answer: A violet fades unless its pigment is witnessed early, so claims must be sealed before they settle. Each identity needs two holders outside its own cluster to countersign its claim, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses instead of one ring. Every claim is priced by rank: the k-th filing costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still requiring unrelated guarantors. A comet audit replays a random claim each epoch; each sealed record carries a sable mark that cannot be pooled or resold.
